raw_case_text:
The patient was a girl aged 4 years and 2 months who was otherwise healthy before presenting with KD symptoms; she had achieved normal developmental milestones and received regular vaccinations. She did not have any relevant medical, psychosocial, or family history. She was admitted to our hospital because she had persistent high fever (<= 38.5 C) for 3 days. Her parents stated that she had first developed diffuse abdominal pain and swelling on the left side of the neck and had initially been taken to a local general practitioner, who suspected acute gastroenterocolitis. Because of the persistent fever and subsequent development of jaundice, she was brought to our hospital for further evaluation. When admitted, she had poor appetite and vomiting and had developed symptoms of respiratory tract infection, such as rhinorrhea and coughing with sputum. Sore throat, dyspnea, diarrhea, constipation, dysuria, and reductions in urine output were not noted.
A physical examination revealed that the patient had a 39 C fever, scleral icterus in both eyes, nonpurulent conjunctival congestion, oral mucosa redness, swelling on the left side of the neck, diffuse abdominal tenderness in the periumbilical area, and crackles in the lungs. Chest X-ray revealed an elevated level of pulmonary infiltrates in both lungs (Figure 1A). Her laboratory data were as follows: hemoglobin = 10.2 (normal range = 11.0-14.5) g/dl, leukocytes = 24,700 (4,000-12,000) 106/L, thrombocytes = 250,100 (130,000-400,000) 106/L, C-reactive protein (CRP) = 14.17 (<1) mg/dl, erythrocyte sedimentation rate = 95 (0-20) mm/h, prothrombin time = 17.3 (11.0-14.5) s, international normalized ratio = 1.32 (<1.20), activated partial thromboplastin time = 45.8 (32.0-45.0) s, aspartate aminotransferase = 489 (15-50) U/L, alanine aminotransferase = 253 (5-45) U/L, total bilirubin = 4.3 (<1.5) mg/dl, direct bilirubin = 2.4 (<0.2) mg/dl, alkaline phosphatase = 337 (134-315) U/L, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase = 145 (5-32) U/L, amylase = 112 (26-115) U/L, lipase = 58 (22-51) U/L, blood urea nitrogen = 11 (5-18) mg/dl, serum creatinine = 0.49 (0.20-0.60) mg/dl, albumin = 3.9 (3.5-5.6) g/dl, ceruloplasmin = 24.2 (20-60) mg/dl, and Cu = 860 (700-1,500) mug/L. Her serological test results revealed positivity for Mycoplasma pneumoniae [M. pneumoniae; immunoglobulin G = 1,810.79 (<100.00) 103U/L and immunoglobulin M = 3,381.64 (<770.00) 103U/L] but negativity for Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, and hepatitis A, B, and C. Furthermore, tests for antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, and antistreptolysin O were negative, as were the results of the influenza A/B and group A streptococcus antigen screening test and pneumococcal urinary antigen testing. Nasal swab and stool tests revealed negative results for adenovirus, and results for rotavirus were also negative. The stool microscopy results were normal. Samples were collected for culture, and the patient was treated with 80 mg/kg ceftriaxone for enteric fever and cholestatic hepatitis and with azithromycin for bronchopneumonia (induced by the M. pneumoniae infection). Treatment response was poor, and the fever persisted. Abdominal ultrasonography indicated acute gastroenterocolitis with ileus and pelvic ascites but without cystic duct or bile duct dilatation. Neck tissue ultrasonography revealed multiple lymphadenopathies on the left side of the neck (largest dimensions: 2.08 cm x 1.49 cm; Figure 1B).
The high fever persisted for 2 days after admission (>5 days total), and a polymorphic skin rash developed, accompanied by lymphadenopathy on the left side of the neck, oral mucosa redness with strawberry tongue, and nonpurulent conjunctival congestion. The patient received a diagnosis of KD, and a single dose of IVIG as a 12-h 2 g/kg intravenous infusion and acetylsalicylic acid (50 mg/kg/day, divided into four doses) was administered. Echocardiography revealed no coronary artery involvement. After the administration of IVIG and aspirin, the fever and abdominal pain subsided and the jaundice and skin rash gradually resolved. Acetylsalicylic acid was reduced to one dose of 3-5 mg/kg at 48 h after the fever had subsided, and liver function improved gradually. Further laboratory examination results are presented in Table 2. The patient was discharged and followed up at our outpatient department. Abnormal laboratory data gradually returned to normal, and the echocardiography results for the coronary arteries in the outpatient department follow-up were normal.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 4-year-2-month-old girl presented with a 3-day history of persistent high fever (>=38.5 °C), diffuse abdominal pain, left neck swelling, and jaundice, accompanied by anorexia, vomiting, rhinorrhea, and productive cough.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially diagnosed with acute gastroenterocolitis by a local practitioner for abdominal pain and left neck swelling, the patient was brought to the hospital when high fever (>=38.5 °C) persisted for 3 days and jaundice appeared. Two days after admission (>5 days of fever), despite empiric intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin, she developed a polymorphic generalized skin rash and strawberry tongue.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy child with normal developmental milestones and up-to-date routine immunizations; unremarkable family and psychosocial history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever, diffuse abdominal pain, left neck swelling, jaundice, anorexia, nonbilious vomiting, rhinorrhea, productive cough, and day 2 polymorphic rash and strawberry tongue.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 39.0 °C, bilateral scleral icterus, bilateral nonpurulent conjunctival congestion, oral mucosal erythema evolving into strawberry tongue on hospital day 2, enlarged left cervical lymphadenopathy, diffuse periumbilical abdominal tenderness, bilateral pulmonary crackles, and a polymorphic skin rash appearing on hospital day 2.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL (ref 11.0-14.5), WBC 24,700 x 10^6/L (ref 4,000-12,000), platelets 250,100 x 10^6/L (ref 130,000-400,000), CRP 14.17 mg/dL (ref <1), ESR 95 mm/h (ref 0-20), PT 17.3 s (ref 11.0-14.5), INR 1.32 (ref <1.20), aPTT 45.8 s (ref 32.0-45.0), AST 489 U/L (ref 15-50), ALT 253 U/L (ref 5-45), total bilirubin 4.3 mg/dL (ref <1.5), direct bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL (ref <0.2), ALP 337 U/L (ref 134-315), GGT 145 U/L (ref 5-32), amylase 112 U/L (ref 26-115), lipase 58 U/L (ref 22-51), BUN 11 mg/dL, creatinine 0.49 mg/dL, albumin 3.9 g/dL, ceruloplasmin 24.2 mg/dL, and serum copper 860 ug/L. Serology was strongly positive for Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM (3,381.64 x 10^3 U/L; ref <770) and IgG (1,810.79 x 10^3 U/L; ref <100), and negative for EBV, cytomegalovirus (CMV), HAV, HBV, HCV, ANA, RF, ANCA, ASO, influenza A/B, Group A streptococcus, urine pneumococcal antigen, and nasal/stool adenovirus and rotavirus. Chest X-ray showed bilateral pulmonary infiltrates; abdominal ultrasound showed ileus and pelvic ascites without biliary dilatation; neck ultrasound showed enlarged left cervical lymph nodes (up to 2.08 x 1.49 cm); baseline and follow-up echocardiograms showed normal coronary arteries.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Kawasaki disease presenting with acute cholestatic hepatitis and triggered by Mycoplasma pneumoniae bronchopneumonia, confirmed by classical clinical Kawasaki criteria, elevated M. pneumoniae IgM (3,381.64 x 10^3 U/L) and IgG (1,810.79 x 10^3 U/L), and exclusion of cytomegalovirus (CMV), EBV, and viral hepatitis A/B/C. Following lack of defervescence on initial ceftriaxone (80 mg/kg) and azithromycin, treatment with a single 12-hour infusion of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG, 2 g/kg) and high-dose oral aspirin (50 mg/kg/day divided QID, stepped down to 3-5 mg/kg/day 48 hours after defervescence) resulted in prompt resolution of fever, jaundice, abdominal pain, and rash, with normal liver function and coronary arteries on follow-up.
